title: Crisp Melted Monterey Jack Cheese Quesadillas with Fresh Tomato Salsa
summary: Flour tortillas filled with Monterey Jack are pan-fried in a little oil until golden and crisp, then cut into wedges and served with a fresh tomato and jalapeño salsa.
equipment: large non-stick frying pan (at least 26 cm)
wire rack set on a baking tray

ingredients.item: Monterey Jack, coarsely grated (check the rennet)

steps.title: Make the salsa
steps.text: Mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, coriander and lime juice in the bowl and set aside. No salt is needed, as the cheese and tortillas carry plenty.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Lay the tortillas flat and scatter 75 g cheese over one half of each, leaving a 1 cm border so it doesn't leak. Fold the other half over and press gently.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Put the rack on its tray in a 100 °C (80 °C fan) oven to keep the first batch warm. Heat 1 tbsp oil in the pan over medium heat until shimmering.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook 2 quesadillas side by side for 2-3 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp. Brush the tops lightly with oil, flip with the spatula and cook for 2 minutes more, until the second side is golden and the cheese has melted completely. Keep them warm on the rack while you cook the other two in the remaining oil.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Rest for 1 minute so the cheese firms slightly, then cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges and serve with the salsa.

tips: Medium heat is key; too hot and the tortilla burns before the cheese melts.
Grate the cheese yourself: pre-grated cheese has anti-caking starch and melts less smoothly.
A wire rack keeps the bases crisp; a plate makes them steam and go soft.
Mild cheddar or a mix of cheddar and mozzarella works if you can't find Monterey Jack.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and use within 3 days; reheat once in a dry pan over medium heat until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
